**Resubmitted — T4C: missing, cured at the preferred level (propose_redline ok:true, minimality ok).**

This round I addressed the verifier's two confirmation points and left the operative drafting stable:

- **(i) Cross-reference verified.** I re-read the source: the retained for-cause preamble sits under heading paragraph p0106 "5.1 Breach", so "Notwithstanding Section 5.1" in the new Section 5.4 resolves correctly and is not dangling. p0106 is now cited in paragraphIds.
- **(ii) "fees" retained deliberately.** The checklist element is "Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata"; swapping to "amounts prepaid" would change the element's noun, which the drafting rules bar. The verifier confirms the descriptive usage does not defeat the element, so I left it and instead flagged the "Price" terminology point for the negotiation, not the operative text.
- **Quote sharpened.** The finding now quotes SOW §6.1 verbatim — the only convenience mechanic in the deal — which demonstrates precisely why the rule is unmet: it reaches Purchase Orders only and still leaves IBM paying cost reimbursements. The §5.1 for-cause sentence remains the verbatim basis for element 4's already_met mapping.

Operative clause unchanged and validated: *"5.4 Termination for Convenience by IBM. Notwithstanding Section 5.1, IBM may terminate this Agreement for its convenience upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to MSL, in which case MSL shall refund to IBM, pro rata, any fees prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination."*

On the recurring deterministic flag: three verifier passes have now inspected the rendered text and each confirmed it expressly contains the IBM convenience right, the 30-day notice and the pro-rata refund, characterising the regex result as a mechanical false negative against the pre-redline baseline — which is expected for a "missing" finding. Any further edit to chase the regex would mean adding terms outside the checklist or importing an undefined "Customer" alias (I confirmed "Customer" is not a defined term here), so I am holding the drafting as validated.
